headline: Antibiotics in feed: bigger pigs, tougher germs
dek: Robert Stokstad and Thomas Jukes, US farms, 1950s on.

slides.label: The bright idea
slides.title: More meat from cheap feed
slides.text: After World War II, US farms struggled to meet demand for meat. **Robert Stokstad and Thomas Jukes hunted for the missing growth factor.**

slides.label: It worked
slides.title: A pinch, a big gain
slides.text: A pinch of the new antibiotic aureomycin made chicks grow faster. **In trials from 1950 to 1985, young pigs gained 16% faster.**

slides.label: The backfire
slides.title: The survivors took over
slides.statLabel: of samples mostly resistant, farm family vs. neighbors (Levy, 1976)
slides.text: A small daily dose kills the bacteria it can reach and spares the ones that resist. **The survivors multiply and pass their resistance on.**

slides.label: Could anyone have seen it coming?
slides.title: Yes, and early
slides.text: In 1945 Alexander Fleming warned that too-small doses teach microbes to resist. **In 1951 a study found resistance in turkeys fed the drug.**

slides.label: The long cleanup
slides.title: Fifty years of phase-outs
slides.text: The EU banned growth promoters in 2006; the US ended growth use of medically important drugs in 2017. **In 2024, US farm sales of those drugs rose 16%.**

slides.label: The ledger
slides.title: Worth it?
gains: Young pigs gained 16% faster and used feed 7% more efficiently, trials 1950 to 1985 (Cromwell, 2002)
A worldwide ban would cut meat output 1.3% to 3%, one 2015 OECD estimate finds
A US ban would cost consumers $1.2 billion to $2.5 billion a year (National Research Council, 1998)
costs: Farm dwellers carrying mostly tetracycline-resistant gut bacteria within six months (Levy, 1976)
72.7% of Danish broiler E. faecium resistant to vancomycin-type drugs in 1995, after avoparcin feed (Aarestrup, 2001)
A gene that defeats last-resort colistin in 21% of farm animals sampled in China, 2011 to 2014 (Lancet Infectious Diseases, 2016)
slides.text: It made meat cheaper to raise. **It also gave bacteria daily practice surviving drugs people need.**

slides.label: Pattern
slides.title: The cure breeds resistance
slides.text: Growth doses were low, daily and given to whole herds. **Bacteria met the drug constantly, at levels some could survive.**

slides.label: Lesson
slides.title: What we take from it
slides.text: A fix aimed at living things is also a test they can learn to pass. **Ask what survives it, and what happens next.**
